rationale: The enterprise schema is explicitly versioned.
Composite identities are qualified by a stable dotted namespace.
Record fields are scalar and unique.
Enum variants are deterministic and unique.
All guarded composite descriptor families have source declarations.
Moves transfer ownership to a distinct named owner.
Shared borrows permit reads until explicit release.
Mutable borrows remain exclusive and explicitly released.
Use after move fails deterministically.
Shared and mutable borrows cannot overlap.
Duplicate record fields fail descriptor validation.
Borrow lifetimes must close before source completion.
Root and vendored packages use exact identity, version and license metadata.
Dependency manifests and reachable sources are cryptographically locked.
Missing local dependencies fail without registry or network fallback.
A prohibited redistributed license cannot enter the graph.
A dependency or package range cannot replace an exact version.
A verified v2 lock and explicit source epoch produce conformant deterministic creation metadata and dependency-manifest references.
C ABI version and status behavior are stable.
Out-of-range slice access returns a stable error.
Malformed UTF-8 cannot create an owned string.
The shared-library export set is exact.
Installed C consumers link static and shared core targets.
Installed C++ consumers use the versioned namespace and RAII wrapper.
